The trend at numerous airports across the nation is to provide direct access from the Interstate System or Expressway System to air terminal facilities. Improved access roads to the airport from the freeway system in other metropolitan areas of like size, such as Dallas/Ft. Worth, Minneapolis/St. Paul, Atlanta and Cincinnati have already recognized this as a necessity.
Rising population and its concentration in Metropolitan Milwaukee have been key factors accounting for the steady increases in both air passengers and cargo traffic. Wisconsin's population will increase from about 4.6 million today to about 6 million in 1990. Most of the increases will probably be in the seven southeastern Wisconsin counties most directly served by the corridor in which this connection is located. The population in these seven counties will increase from the present total of more than 1.8 million to 2.3 million in 1990, an increase of 30%. Milwaukee is the 19th largest metropolitan area in the United States and is served by an airport that is the 70th busiest in the nation. Figure 14 shows that passenger traffic has increased consistently at General Mitchell Field over the past ten years. The projected growth of air passenger traffic from over 1,600,000 in 1968 to 5,400,000 in 1990 indicates that vehicular access to the airport as it exists would become inefficient in the near future. Air cargo is expected to quadruple from its tonnage now to the year 1990.
